display_name: Shankaran, Kerala Almanac Maker of Calicut
one_line: A learned panchanga maker and practical astronomer working in the busy ports and temples of the Malabar Coast.

appearance.age_look: early 30s, lean but sturdy from walking between port, temple, and households
appearance.face: oval face, medium-brown Malabar complexion, straight nose, neatly trimmed black moustache, small tilak of sandal paste on the forehead, thoughtful eyes with a calm default expression
appearance.hair: thick black hair parted slightly to the right, gathered into a short, tidy knot at the back of the head; simple white cotton headband tied around the crown, leaving the knot visible
appearance.costume: era-accurate Namboodiri-style scholar attire: a cream-white handwoven cotton dhoti (mundu) wrapped to ankle length with a broad golden border (kasavu) and a neat front pleat, worn with a fitted short-sleeved off-white cotton angavastram-style upper cloth that covers the torso and ties at the side; over this, a saffron-bordered light brown cotton shawl draped over the left shoulder and across the chest; simple leather sandals; on his wrists, thin copper bangles; a palm-leaf manuscript cord slung diagonally like a strap; modest, practical textiles with subtle stripe patterns, no lavish embroidery.
appearance.signature: a neatly rolled bundle of palm-leaf almanac manuscripts bound with red cotton cord, with a small wooden stylus tucked into the wrap, carried in his left hand or slung at his hip

ref_desc: Shankaran is a medium-brown, moustached Malabar scholar with a short-knot black hairstyle and white headband, wearing cream-gold bordered dhoti, off-white upper cloth, light brown saffron-edged shawl and sandals, carrying a red-corded palm-leaf almanac bundle with wooden stylus, in cream, gold, brown, saffron and red tones.
sheet_prompt: Full-body anime-style character: depict Shankaran, a Malabar Coast almanac maker, standing front-facing in a neutral pose. He has an oval medium-brown face, calm thoughtful eyes, straight nose, neat black moustache and a small sandalwood tilak on his forehead. His hair is thick black, parted slightly right, gathered into a short tidy knot at the back of his head, encircled by a simple white cotton headband. He wears a cream-white cotton dhoti (mundu) to the ankles with a broad golden border and a crisp front pleat, plus a fitted off-white short-sleeved upper cloth that fully covers his torso and ties at the side. Over this, drape a light brown cotton shawl with a saffron-orange border over his left shoulder and across his chest. Add thin copper bangles on his wrists and plain leather sandals on his feet. Across his body runs a simple cord suggesting how he carries manuscripts. In his left hand or at his hip, show his signature prop: a tightly rolled bundle of palm-leaf almanac manuscripts bound with deep red cotton cord, a small wooden stylus tucked into the wrap. Use a palette of cream white for garments, golden yellow for dhoti borders, light brown for the shawl, saffron orange for edging, and deep red for the manuscript cord, keeping the look modest, scholarly, and rooted in 14th–16th century Malabar port and temple culture.
